question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{30}$ be a random sample of size $n=30$ from a population with probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3}, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.03,$ calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}>0.7).$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-3.2\,$ | $\,0.0006\,$ | $\,0.0006\,$ | $\,0.0006\,$ |
| $\,-3.1\,$ | $\,0.0008\,$ | $\,0.0008\,$ | $\,0.0008\,$ |
| $\,-3.0\,$ | $\,0.0012\,$ | $\,0.0011\,$ | $\,0.0011\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =30,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot 4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{4{x}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4}{5} \\  & =0.8,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.03.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0.8,\frac{0.03}{30}) \\  & ∼N(0.8,0.001).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>0.7).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>0.7) & =P(Z>\frac{0.7-0.8}{\sqrt{0.001}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-3.16)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the complement of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>-3.16) & =1-P(Z<-3.16) \\  & =1-Φ(-3.16).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have that

$$
Φ(-3.16)=0.0008.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>0.7) & =1-Φ(-3.16) \\  & =1-0.0008 \\  & =0.9992.\end{aligned}
$$
